title: onepage-adjunct-coverage-compact-jul-2029
body:
One-page adjunct coverage compact (working tracker)

Quick summary:
- Small, highly actionable tracker for patch / small rollout weekend coverage and one-off integrations.
- Purpose: unify owners, surface blockers, and give a quick run-rate estimate (ops + GPU) so product + SRE can decide on manual vs automated fallback.
- Not authoritative — copy into a formal runbook if we escalate.

Context:
- Trigger: unexpected increase in dedup/embedding re-rank jobs in eu-west-1 starting 2029-07-10. Some customers hit higher tail latencies; product asked for manual coverage plan for next 72h.
- Quick ask from PMs: can we grant 3 days of manual surge coverage with an explicit rollback plan and cost cap.

Tracker table (light spreadsheet view):

Row | Area | Owner | Priority | ETA/Window | Current blocker | Manual coverage steps | Fallback route | Est. GPU-hours/day | Contingency contact
----|------|-------|----------|------------|-----------------|-----------------------|----------------|--------------------|-------------------
1 | Embeddings pipeline | Priya Sharma | P0 | 7/11 09:00-18:00 UTC | KV cache invalidations after model swap | Pause downstream async re-rank, route reads to read-only cache snapshot, operator-run warmup sequence (see steps) | Route to smaller model-quant (m3q) + degrade to 50% perf | "~18h" | oncall-eng-sre
2 | Hosted API routes | Jordan Lee | P1 | 7/11 12:00-20:00 UTC | Rate-limit thresholds not hitting; unclear burst config | Temporarily lift per-customer caps for core customers, monitor burn | Canary region eu-central fallback | "~6h" | PM-product-hosted-api
3 | Dedicated customers (acct-553) | Marta Novak | P0 | immediate | Data isolation policy prevents cross-account bursting | Deliver hot-path escalate doc to AE + schedule direct connector swap window | Dedicated pool failover to spare node group | "~24h" | Account-SE
4 | Observability dashboard | Luca Moretti | P2 | 7/11 08:00-16:00 UTC | Missing latency slices for cold-cache | Add ad-hoc span tagging + throwaway dashboard; retain for 48h | N/A | "~1h infra" | observability-oncall

Notes on manual coverage steps (short actionable checklist):
- Operator warmup sequence (Priya): 
  1) Stop consumer for 60s, flush prefix cache to snapshot, verify checksums.
  2) Bring up 2 warm nodes with quant-profile beta-3.
  3) Run 2x synthetic load at 10% expected to validate KV behavior (use runner/quick-runner job id 789).
  4) If tail p95 > target for > 10m, rollback to model v2029-06-29.

- Rate-limit lift (Jordan):
  - Slack: #hosted-api-ops -> post intent + timebox.
  - Use console overrides: route.override.cap.customer=core-customers list.
  - Watch token burn metric and set automated revert alarm (if spend > $1.2k/day).

Back-of-envelope economics (very quick):
- GPU-hours/day estimate method: sum of per-flow warm node hours + synthetic test windows. Conservative buffer +20%.
- Estimated incremental cost for 72h of manual coverage: ~ $3.1k (GPU + SRE overtime), split: 70% infra, 30% people. (Use for quick go/no-go).

Open questions / decision points (flagged for PM/Eng leads):
- Do we accept temporary per-customer cap removal for top-10 customers? (PM ask)
- Is the dedicated account comfortable with node failover that shifts to shared spare pool (policy exception needed)?
- Do we want to run quant-profile beta-3 in production or prefer model rollback?

Quick log (time ordered actions):
- 07/11 07:50: initial alert from observability (p95 embeddings up 1.8x)
- 07/11 08:05: Pager triggered, SRE triaged, declared potential P1 for embeddings
- 07/11 08:25: Quick sync with PM/product -> decision to assemble this compact tracker and propose manual 72h coverage
- 07/11 08:43: Priya started warmup sequence (step 1).
- 07/11 09:12: Warm nodes up, running synthetic checks (id 789), initial p95 drop seen.

Next actions (owners, actionable):
- Priya: finish warmup sequence, confirm KV snapshot integrity by 11:00 UTC (owner update in Slack).
- Jordan: prepare cap-lift plan + console overrides by 11:30 UTC; set automated revert alarm.
- Marta: coordinate with Account-SE for dedicated account permission for failover; capture sign-off in ticket JIRA-4382.
- Luca: publish ad-hoc dashboard and link in this doc; keep retention 48h then delete.

Decisions (so far):
- Temporary manual coverage approved for top-10 customers, timeboxed to 72h, cost cap $3.5k (PM verbal).
- Beta quant-profile allowed in warm nodes only; production traffic only after clear pass on synthetic tests.

Notes-to-self / rough things to move to Confluence if we formalize:
- Turn operator warmup steps into a small playbook (confluence page id placeholder).
- Add a tiny runbook snippet for "cap-lift -> automated revert" pattern.

Misc quick links & refs:
- Confluence quick-fallback: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/quick-fallback-playbook
- MR: gitlab.com/redwood/runtime/-/merge_requests/1123 (quant-profile beta-3)
- Jira: JIRA-4382 (dedicated acct-553 failover)
- Slack: #hosted-api-ops, #observability, @oncall-eng-sre

End of compact tracker. Keep this doc as transient working artifact; if we escalate, create formal runbook in Confluence and link back.

(edit notes) 07/12: Marta added dedicated account sign-off placeholder; Jordan added cost cap comment.
